utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, good morning, everyone. Yes, Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President, Your Honours. May I introduce Ms. Svitlana Tsukanova, who is from the Ukraine, has an LLM from Radboud University, Nijmegen, in European Union law and international law. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning, Mr. Harvey. You're not hiding anymore from my eyesight. Sorry, I meant Mr. Tieger. Yes, Mr. Karadzic, can you see Mr. Kovac without any difficulty in terms of your eye sight?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Excellency. Thank you. Mr. Lazarevic was very kind to take care of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Yes. Good morning, Mr. Nicholls, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. I don't want to spend a lot of time on it because it's in your statement at paragraphs 111 to 113. Actually, would you mind putting your statement down or turning it over. I would like you to ask me when you need to refer to it to refresh your memory. In other words, could you just not use your statement unless you ask me first. You can refer to it now, if you want, but after that, please put it down. I'm talking about the 10 July order, P02992. Putting the RS MUP --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm not sure Mr. Kovac understood what you said.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Kovac, you don't need to rely on your statement in answering Mr. Nicholls's question. When you need to -- when you would to read your statement, the Chamber would allow you to do so at any time. Let's continue. Yes, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: If I may assist my learned colleague, paragraph 119 of Mr. Kovac's statement does not refer to this. It's something completely different, so maybe this could resolve this confusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, 111 to 113, that's what I'm talking about. But you don't need to read it. I'm asking you about RS MUP order 6495. We can bring it up, P02992. Now, you've talked about this in your statement, I don't want to go over your explanation again. What I want to ask you about is your prior testimony about this document. This is from your testimony in the Medic case at page 52 in English, B/C/S page 39. Asked about this document, you said, "I left this area," as you say in your statement here, "but the president of the republic directly called Karisik, my deputy, and Borovcanin and dictated to them this order." Do you stand by that testimony you gave in the state court?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do but I wish to clarify. I don't know that I said that President Karadzic had called Karisik and Borovcanin. He issued the order which was in keeping with his constitutional powers. And it was forwarded to the MUP institution where Karisik and Borovcanin were. That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: One moment. All right. Let's just bring up your testimony. 65 ter 25514, in your language should be page 39. I'll read out from the English again. "I left this area, but the president of the republic directly called Karisik, my deputy, and Borovcanin and dictated to them this order."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Let's locate the passage.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: It should be -- if that is the correct page -- I can't find it in the Cyrillic, I'm sorry, but that's the correct page and it's above where we see item 4 at the bottom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you see the passage, Mr. Kovac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Wait. Wait. Do you see the passage? Have you found the part I read out? That's the question: Have you found it and read it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Of course it indicates the passage.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Did you say that in this trial, as recorded there?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think this was recorded precisely but I will testify today how it was, that the essence is the same, the order was passed on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. I understand that. I'm just asking you, this is a recording of your prior testimony, if you stand by that sworn testimony, or if you have something different to say in the sworn testimony today?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not saying any different today. I said at the beginning when you asked me whether I stand by my statements, I do. About this formulation, I don't know what you want. The essence is the same. It's just the formulation. The president issued the order in writing.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] I'm not asking you that. I know that. I'm asking you if you said that under oath, what is recorded there by their recording equipment.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm not sure that this was recorded exactly word for word, but the essence is the same. It's clear. It's clear that the president issued the order to Karisik and Borovcanin at the MUP. I wasn't there. I don't know what you want to draw from this.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Let me tell you what your deputy, Karisik, testified about this order and this claim of yours just a few months ago on 27 June in this courtroom. I read out precise -- first of all, this is at T40605 to 40606, lines 15 to 20 on those pages. First of all, he said that when he met with President Karadzic on 10 July, he didn't know or discuss the order, and I read out to him your testimony that I've just read out to you precisely and asked if that helped him remember that you say it was he who was involved in this order. And he said, No, no, I refute Tomo Kovac's statement. I think he got confused there. It's possible that the president ordered someone, and goes on, and then says, I was dealing with Sarajevo. I was not there. I was dealing with Sarajevo. As for the problems concerning Srebrenica, it's only Mr. Kovac who can speak about that, so you can ask him when he comes. I deny this. So both you and your subordinate Karisik are running from any involvement in the passage of this order; right?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would not accept your assertion about evasion. In all my earlier statements and interactions with you and the Office of the Prosecutor, I did not act like that, but let us clarify. You are not allowing me now, and you did not allow me earlier, to state clearly what happened here in essence. President Karadzic issued an order, passed it on to the MUP institution. At the MUP, Borovcanin received the order through MUP services. As for Karisik, I don't know whether he saw it the first or the second day, whether he passed it on. As my deputy, he had insight into it, I cannot go into that, but that order was issued in keep with the law, and it had to be followed. The fact that I wasn't there and what my motivations were changes nothing to the execution of this order and that's perfectly clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That's not my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let me help you. Mr. Kovac, according to your testimony in the Medic case, it's recorded you said that Mr. Karadzic called Karisik directly and issued this order.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot remember exactly now all these details, but as far as I recollect, and even this order that was given, you have original documents, I don't know why you didn't provide original documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Kovac, let me ask you again. But you said today that the essence was the same. So do you agree that Mr. Karadzic issued that order directly to Mr. Karisik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He didn't have any reason to issue the order directly to Karisik, he issued it to the institution, and he gave this order to the MUP. Who actually received it and how they passed it on is technical matter. Now, to give different explanation 20 years on, I can't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: This isn't 20 years on. This is your testimony from 2006, and at that point you said it was issued directly to Karisik. And I am not asking you about the way orders are issued, I'm pointing out to you your testimony now, if we listen to what you say today, your testimony in the prior case wasn't true, was it? You don't stand by it. You just make it up when you were testifying in the state court.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not accept that I made anything up. At that time Karisik was my deputy Staff Commander and he could have accepted it. Even I myself didn't know who passed the order on until I saw documents in The Hague. I thought at that time it was Karisik but it was a different member of the staff, as I learned later, who received the document and passed it on. I saw the original document after I testified the first time, and I saw it here at The Hague Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And it was signed by another member of the command staff; right?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. Now, you'll agree with me that at least 12 members of those MUP forces put into the Srebrenica theatre by the order we have just been talking about have been convicted of murders at Kravica, Sandici, three days later; right? Three days after this order was issued.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably. I don't know what you are driving at.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You testified in their trials. Probably? Can I have P06378.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did, but -- yes, I did, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: While we are waiting for that to come up, are you aware that Goran Saric has recently been indicted for murders at Kravica, Sandici and Cerska for genocide? Goran Saric is Special Police commander.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's one in a series of indictments brought by default. I don't know what you want to put to me with this indictment against Saric.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, then just -- just listen a minute. The reason was I asked you if people who had been put into the combat zone pursuant to this order had been convicted of crimes they committed three days later --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The speakers are overlapping. Kindly pause between questions and answer. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: My apologies.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: At Kravica and Sandici. Just look at it quickly. You know that men put into combat by this order committed crimes, have been convicted of committing crimes, genocide, three days later; right?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is completely inaccurate. You are changing everything. Those people were convicted because the people who commanded them on the ground did it badly. It's not true that they were indicted because of this order. The order was issued in keeping with the law.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That's not my question and I'll move on. All right. I'm moving on to 12 July and some of the things you start doing in relation to the Srebrenica operation. You recall -- could I just quickly have P02995. And this you'll remember it, it's your 12 July 1995 order, type signed by you, forwarding President Karadzic's order to establish the police station in Srebrenica and some other points. Can we go to the second page for Mr. Kovac in the Serbian. So you sent this order; right? This is your order?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Officially it's signed Tomislav Kovac, but why don't you produce the original document? I didn't sign this document. I'm not questioning the lawfulness of this document, but I didn't sign it. It's not a copy, but it's a totally different typed document. If you find the original you will see that I did not sign it, but I'm not questioning the lawfulness of this. I'm not questioning anything from this order.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Right. My only point is -- and we don't need to go through the order. Is this -- I know this is not a signed copy but you forwarded this order from Mr. Karadzic on the 12th of July; right?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I did not forward it. My services forwarded it, somebody from the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. I'll try to be clear. When I say "you," I don't mean you personally operating the teleprinter, I mean it is type signed by you as Staff Commander. As deputy minister, rather. Okay. And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Yes, please go on, Mr. Kovac.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's correct that it's written deputy minister, but I'm saying once again that I didn't sign this, which means it didn't pass through my hands. But I'm not questioning the lawfulness or anything from this document. There is nothing there that is contrary to the law.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. This is taking longer than I want. Do you agree that this came from your office with your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It went out of my office but not with my knowledge because physically I wasn't there when this was forwarded.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. In your 2003 interview, which is 65 ter 22146, with the Office of the Prosecutor of The Hague, at pages 83 to 84 of the English and 90 to 91 of the Serbian, you said, in answer to the question: "What happened on the 12th? "Tomo Kovac: Okay. On the 12th, I remember there was an overload of dispatches, and so on, and on that day we also received the order from the president, Radovan Karadzic, on forming of the police station, and I believe we have taken certain steps to -- this is the order I would like to comment on." The investigator says: "Go ahead. The order is -- just for the record, the order is KP 1407/95. That's the order we have as ERN 01134170, the same one I just showed you." And you say: "Okay, what I want to say is what you can notice just looking at the form in the way this has been composed because it's come from my office with my knowledge, as opposed to the office which -- as opposed to the order which was issued, you know, outside the office and without my knowledge." And then you go on to talk about how you can tell it's authentic. So, in 2003, when you were telling us the truth you said it came from your office with your knowledge, why are you giving a different answer when I ask you exactly the same question today?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not giving you a different answer. I said we received at my office more than one of these documents, and after this, I managed to get ahold of some documents where you will see again that I did not sign this one because I wasn't physically there. When I said "we received," I meant the ministry. We received several documents. And I clearly pointed out that this document passed through the protocol of the minister's office.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Stop.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Stop. Because I don't want to take the time to try to have to impeach you on every single question I ask you, but my question to you was not about the process, my question was I read out exactly the same language from the interview that this came from your office with your knowledge. And you said, no. Then I show you your interview where you say, It came from the office with my knowledge, in response to a non-leading question, and now you're telling me those answers are the same.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I believe my answers are completely the same and all the essence of all these events in my explanations in these documents changes nothing to the problem of Srebrenica and the engagement of MUP forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yeah, well, I'd ask you to use -- try to be a little more precise because you keep going back to these broad topics when I ask you about things you've said. And you think your answers are completely the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do we have the correct page which says that that order came from his office with his knowledge? Where is it? Yes, Mr. Kovac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it's unclear to me too. Since the original -- since the Tribunal has the original documents, why does the Prosecutor not come up with the original documents now? Because at that time --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That's not important. You talked to the investigator that that order came out -- was issued with your knowledge and now you deny it. So I want -- the Chamber just wants to know what's the truth, whether we have the original or not.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me explain why I'm asking for the originals. In the originals one can see exactly who signed what, and there is no dilemma there, who stands by which document.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I didn't ask you one question about your signature. I've not asked you one question about your signature in my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'll move on, I think. Okay. Can we look at P02996 quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: What this is, it's from Dragomir Vasic, the Zvornik CJB chief. It's a reply to the dispatch we just looked at and talked about for a while about whether it went with your knowledge or not. And it says, acting -- it says RE dispatch number KP/-1-407/95 of 12 July 1995, the one we just looked at: Acting in accordance with your dispatch, I contacted the civilian commissioner in Bratunac, Miroslav Deronjic. And as you -- as you requested in Mr. Karadzic's order, and then he discusses the meeting he had. So you are on 12 July forwarding Karadzic's order which says to establish co-operation with Deronjic and ask for reports on the situation and you're getting them the same day; right? Reports from your subordinate, Vasic.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We were not interested in Deronjic's activity. As far as I can see -- well, we didn't even write this dispatch. We say that this has to do with contact with Deronjic in relation to the establishment of the station, and we did not need any reports about Deronjic's activity in the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I don't know if there is a communication problem. I was saying Vasic is reporting to you. One of the things he's reporting is that he established contact with Miroslav Deronjic which was part of your order that we just looked at. Vasic is reporting to you about what Vasic is doing; right?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But skillfully, very skillfully, you've been moving towards me, not only today but for ten years now, to have me confirm that the ministry is linked to Deronjic and his activities. And you said once that we were receiving reports about Deronjic's activities. I said that that is not correct and that is not within our purview and we were not interested.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In line 24, that's the misunderstanding, [In English] Deronjic asked for the reports. [Interpretation] It turns out that the reports were sought from Deronjic. And then when we receive a translation of that, it sounds even more like that -- like it's Deronjic who is supposed to provide these reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, it says "Reports from your subordinate, Vasic," on line 25. So I don't think it was that unclear. And Mr. Vasic reports to you - forget about Deronjic for a minute - about a meeting with Mladic and Krstic. In number 4 we get to the establishment of the police station. In point 5 that a meeting will begin at 10.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you check with the witness whether he can read the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Can you read the document, Mr. Kovac? Do you need it blown up?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indiscernible]

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I have a hard copy, if you want one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, that would be more convenient.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That a meeting will begin at 10.00 with representatives of UNPROFOR, that already a hundred trailer trucks have been provided for transport. And number 6, joint police forces are advancing on Potocari with the aim of taking UNPROFOR personnel prisoner, surrounding the entire population, and clearing the terrain of enemy groups. Number 8, you'll be promptly informed of all further facts and developments. So my very simple question is in -- again in response to the order we just saw you sending out, Mr. Karadzic's order and your order, you're getting reports right away from Mr. Vasic; right?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I mean, I'm receiving -- I mean, he's sending reports about overall activities. One order was sent to him about setting up the police station, which is within our purview. This other part doesn't have to do with our purview. He could have informed us. We just asked him to do one thing and that had to do with the establishment of the police station in Srebrenica. All the rest does not fall within the purview of the MUP, within the powers of the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: My question was: Vasic is reporting to you. I didn't ask you again about the power or purview of the MUP, it's that Vasic is reporting to you in response to your order. Part of your order was establish contact with Deronjic, he's responding that he has; part of your order was about the police station, he's responding; and he's explaining to you, as you say, what is happening in Srebrenica on the ground; right?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. The establishment of the station, yes, but this is far wider reporting about the activities of Mladic, UNPROFOR, Deronjic. And that doesn't have to do with our purview, our order, or --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Stop. I think -- it's hard to believe you can't understand these questions since you made it to minister of the interior when were you under 40. Vasic is reporting to you on the situation on the ground.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: There is no part of my question that is about the purview of the MUP.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please. There is no reason for you -- I mean, I've spent a lot of time with you. There is no reason for you to say that I don't understand about what came from the MUP. I mean, I do not have the characteristics of a retard, as you've been putting it. I have this attitude towards you because for ten years now you've been trying to impute things to us, to the MUP, lawfully and unlawfully, to involve us in this, and you're not going to be successful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't understand if we use-- why we waste a lot of time for this. Could you make your question a bit simpler? Mr. Kovac, do you agree that the MUP at the time received this Vasic's report?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the MUP received the report. The MUP has to receive it. If it was sent electronically, it has to be received. That is not being contested. What is being contested --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Kovac, your answer could be either yes or no, so your answer is yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we continue, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And I'm going to skip ahead, but you may recall you got another -- that another report was sent to the MUP from Vasic after the meeting which General Mladic and UNPROFOR --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Kindly speak into the microphone, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: UNPROFOR and some of the Muslims from Potocari. And I'd like to now look at P04934. This is again 12th July. It is type signed by you as Staff Commander. It's from the RS MUP police force staff Pale. It's an order: In order to take over urgent tasks of mopping up the terrain in the Srebrenica sector, I hereby, 1, urgently dispatch all available guide dogs, guides with police dogs, to Srebrenica sector; 2, upon arrival, in Srebrenica contact Ljubisa Borovcanin, deputy commander, who commands the police forces in Srebrenica and make arrangements on what to do next. This order is sent from the MUP staff on the 12th; right?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: It is sending additional police troops to Srebrenica; right?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obviously that can be seen from this, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: It is an order to take over urgent tasks of mopping up the terrain; right?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably such a request was received. Now, what they did on the ground is for the military and for Ljubisa Borovcanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: My point is, yesterday, and in your statement, you say that the MUP was requested to come in just for show so that the Supreme Commander could get some credit for Srebrenica. Yesterday, when I asked you about your prior testimony, you also said that you testified that the MUP wasn't even needed in Srebrenica because there was no resistance, it was over, and they were needed so badly in Sarajevo. In fact, as you just said, there was a request for more forces, and those forces were urgently sent to supplement the troops that President Karadzic sent in; right? That's what we can see from this document.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, again, I claim that it was not necessary for the MUP forces to go to Srebrenica except for some particular police work, to protect roads and to protect the population. That is clear for anyone who dealt with analysing Srebrenica. It was not necessary in relation to the forces that were there. The MUP forces were not needed as combat forces, as police forces to protect roads, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And what's going on on the 12th? We saw Mr. Vasic's report to the MUP just a minute ago, about how the joint MUP forces were going in to surround UNPROFOR -- to surrender the entire civilian protection -- population, take UNPROFOR prisoner. This is the day that the first -- the day that the shipping out of the entire population of the enclave starts. That's what you send the MUP in to assist with, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That's not right. And in the command part we did not take part and we did not carry out these activities. That's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, you also just said that the police -- "... MUP forces were not needed as combat forces, as police forces to protect roads, yes." What you urgently send them in for is mopping up the terrain. You don't urgently send them in to protect a road.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is your assertion. In an area of 50 to 100 kilometres away from Srebrenica, we had movement of armed soldiers. We had to protect the Milici-Zvornik road, as far as police work is concerned. As far as military work is concerned, where the police was placed under their command, I did not go into the way they were being used because they were under their command.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: State security is part of the MUP - right? - under Dragan Kijac?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, one of the entities, separate organisational unit within the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes. Now, we have already seen, and I don't want to talk about it, but I'm sure you know, you'll agree with me that the MUP forces were amongst the very first to enter Potocari; right? You know that?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. I don't think that they were the first to enter Potocari. I think this is an arbitrary assertion. I was not in command there. I did not deal with that. We can talk about that subsequently.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We did not hear the end of the sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Stop. I'm not asking you whether you're in command. I'm asking you factually if you knew that the MUP were among the first into Potocari, and you said you don't know. At that point you answered the question. Can I have P04388. This is a Drina Corps document, not a MUP document. It's from the security chief, Popovic, on 12 July. He explains - maybe this will help you remember - MUP forces entered Potocari in the morning without combat. But the part I want you to look at is number 3. Last sentence: We are separating men from 17 to 60 years of age and we are not transporting them. We have about 70 of them so far and the security organs and state security are working with them. So one part of the MUP goes into Potocari in the morning, men are separated, they are not transported, and state security is "working with them"; right?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This activity was not conducted. I mean, none of these activities that are referred to were conducted by the MUP. It was the security organ, and the operation was under their control and command. Now, individuals who had been resubordinated, whether they had been involved in certain activities, well, that is certainly visible, but this has no link to any kind of order issued by the Ministry of the Interior and this was not under our control.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, as you've said, and as the law shows I don't want to go into it, take the time, the MUP can only be put into combat by an order from the president and the minister. But you're not seriously suggesting that state security was subordinated to the VRS during Srebrenica operation, are you?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, state security, one or two men who were in that area, I don't see -- I mean, I don't know of their activity, that they did anything in that area. From this document I see this now, and I don't -- I didn't know that they did anything in Srebrenica. I was not aware of their activities except for the information that we received about combat movements in the broader area. I was not aware of any other activities. This is minor. In this entire area, there was only one or two members of state security.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm not sure, Mr. Kovac, you answered the question. You said about the resubordination, do you say these DB members were resubordinated to the military at the time? DB, state security.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the time, they were not resubordinated to the army. And I'm not aware of their activity, and I think that as regards their activity, there wasn't really -- well, as far as we, the ministry, are concerned, well, this is a department that is separate, and we did not, I mean, receive such information. And I don't think that they were directly -- I mean, except for their activities in the area, regular activities, reporting, I cannot explain that. I don't know about their activity at the time. I did not receive any information about where they were and what they were doing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That being the case, Mr. Kovac, why did you mention about resubordination at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Resubordination? Because there were official units there that were resubordinate to the army. That was the special unit and -- and the first company from the security centre of Zvornik. And, according to the president's order, they were resubordinated to the army, and there, in accordance with that order, they were present there and they operated under the command of Ljubisa Borovcanin, or rather, the command of the corps commander, the commander of the Drina Corps, so they were there on the basis of that order and they were active on the basis of that order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: After Mr. Nicholls read out this passage, including the activities, alleged activities of DB members, you talked about resubordination. Was it out of your mistake?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no. What was being referred to here was not only state security. Also, other units were mentioned there that were resubordinated according to the order. However, the SDB in terms of how it acts, it is a separate department, it is a separate entity, and their activity was always under certain, I mean, supervision of the head of the State Security Service. I'm not sure. I don't know that they were involved in this area in this way. I do not have that kind of information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Please continue, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Again, though, state security, Dragan Kijac, is part of the MUP, it's under the minister; right?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, they are a unit that is separate, so the State Security Service formally is under the MUP, but they independently carry out -- but --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay, go ahead. Go ahead. They independently carry out? Do you want to say anything more?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there is not anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They -- I mean, their activity is well known. It is a special kind of activity. Certainly they had tasks of their own, but that they worked on the separation of the population, I'm not aware of that information, and I don't think that this information is correct. This is incorrect information of the lieutenant-colonel and --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I didn't ask you at this point about separations. Now, you said, I cannot explain that earlier, when asked by His Honour Judge Kwon about information, I did not receive any information about where they were and what they were doing. Is that serious assertion, Mr. Kovac? You did not receive any information about what -- where state security were and what they were doing? Let's confine it to July 12, 13, 14, 15.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We received information from state security, in general terms. Now, where they were individually and what they did, we did not receive that. Their work was secret, who was where at which point in time and who was doing what. We did receive information. I mean, please don't twist this. We did receive information from state security. That is correct. Now, where they were in terms of groups, individuals, their chief, who was where, if that's what you're asking me, I don't know, but as an institution we did receive reports from them regularly.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. You are Dragan Kijac's boss in July 1995; right? You are superior to him in the MUP chain?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, from the position of deputy minister, except in formal terms, no. The deputy minister could not command the State Security Service. You see from all of this that I was at the level of public security. I mean, if you want me to inform you where Dragan Kijac was at the time, he was on annual leave, on vacation at the seaside, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Where did I ask you about where Dragan Kijac was at the time in my question? Why did you come up with that when I asked if you were his boss?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I started saying that because you've been tendentiously saying that I know where his operatives were and I told you where he was specifically at the time. As for commanding and controlling him and the State Security Service, I could not do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: P04389, please. Skip ahead. So let me just ask you this before we look at this document. You didn't know that Goran Radovic, head of the Bijeljina state security centre, went down to Bratunac on 12, 13 July?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know. He didn't need to inform me and I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You didn't know that Mile Renovica, the Zvornik chief of state security, was in Bratunac on the night of 13 July -- or, in that period, 12, 13 July?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not know. It was normal for him to be in that area because that's his area, that's the area where he was working, Bratunac was our territory and had been before. It's quite normal. It's his daily activity to move around that area. If he did that before, why wouldn't he do it during those days? But he didn't need to report to me about that. He didn't need to inform me because we are not organisationally linked. It was quite normal for him to be in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: This is 13 July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, sorry. Your Honours, I may end up asking for more time - I'm sorry - based on the lengths and type of answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You say he's not organisationally linked to you? He's a state security chief for Zvornik which is part of the MUP which is linked to you as deputy minister of the MUP.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You should not emphasise the position which is just an alternative to the deputy minister. They are linked to the minister and the ministry. I just stood in for the minister in connection with this area. I'm not saying they are not part of the MUP but they are a separate system and, of course, the MUP is kept informed but they are a separate system with separate rules of work.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Nobody has contested that that they are a separate chain. All right. This document is the one for 13 July 1995 from state security, signed by Dragan Kijac. If we go to the second page, Mr. Kovac. And it is headed, to deputy minister of the interior, personally. You, on 13 July 1995, were deputy minister of the interior personally, correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was deputy.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. And so the second person this goes to is to head of public security personally. That's Kijac, right -- Karisik, right?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not Kijac and Karisik, just Karisik.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: My mistake. All right. And this is informing you personally that during the night of 12 to 13, members of the VRS and MUP managed to capture a large number of Muslim soldiers in ambushes set up in the general Konjevic Polje area; right?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And it is informing you of the break-up of some of the Muslim extremist groups as they move along the road. And then it says: "The operation to detect and neutralise the Muslim groups is continuing. Earlier information regarding their intentions and the axes of movement towards Kladanj and Tuzla (Buljim, Pobudje Konjevic Polje, Kaldrmica, Cerska, Snagovo, Crni Vrh) have been confirmed many times in interviews with prisoners." And it talks about Naser Oric. So state security -- excuse me. Let me read one more. Ibgan Mustafic, a former SDA deputy and a former BH assembly and a great opponent of Naser Oric, was among the prisoners and can, with the necessary preparation, be used well in the media. So state security is informing you that they know the movements of the Muslims through many times in interviews with prisoners; right?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I jumped ahead to that. Let's go back to something now on the 12th of July, that Mr. Borovcanin testified to in this courtroom in June. He was asked, excuse me, this is at -- this is 7 June, 39456, at line 5: "Just looking at your after-action report is what I call it, you stated there on the 12th that you received information from the state security employees about the movement of the Muslim column; is that correct? "Inter alia, I received information from them, that is true. "And, who, do you remember their names, these state security folks? "I think I mentioned it in my interview. There were two state security operatives there. One of them was Vito Tomic, the other, last name was Glogovac, I believe. "Sinisa? Sinica Glogovac? "Yes. "And where were they when you received information from them, and where were you in Potocari and what date? "12 July 1995." So let me just recap this a bit. MUP joint MUP forces, as Vasic reported to you, entered Srebrenica, entered Potocari, and take it early on the 12th without resistance. State security is present in Potocari interviewing separated prisoners and getting information. Borovcanin gets information of the movement of the column from state security and then sets up the line to ambush those men in the Muslim column. You still say MUP was not necessary on 12, 13 July, for the operation against Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I still say that, but you are putting other things here, and twisting everything and presenting the MUP as acting independently, that Vasic commanded, that Ljubisa executed and that it was all connected with state security. The state security was not there according to establishment. It was there in the area in accordance with the methodology of work. And like all secret services in the world, they did their work. They were not within the same chain. There was no link with Ljubisa Borovcanin. The fact that they knew each other and exchanged information is their business, their work on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, sorry, their business, their work on the ground, Borovcanin in his report, which I do not want to bring up at the moment, says that on the basis of information from state security, he learned about the movements of the Muslim column which is why he went and set up his positions on the road. That's what he was being questioned about in the transcript reference I read you. So the link there is state security is finding information from prisoners and providing that to the commander of the MUP forces in Srebrenica. What do you mean there is no link?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness's microphone is off.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is no link. As for the assertion that MUP created such an organisation, Ljubisa was under the command of the army. Under the law, Ljubisa was supposed to get information through the security organ of the army. The fact that that he personally knew these people there, that the state security people got information from that area, they obtained that information because they knew each other. Ljubisa used to be -- to know the chief of police in Bratunac. Through the establishment, he was supposed to get information from the security organs of the army while working in that area, because he had been detached, seconded from the MUP, and he was under the command of the army. What he did was not in accordance with the law.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. So let me get it straight. Your explanation is that Borovcanin is in Potocari, Sinisa Glogovac is in Potocari, they recognise each other from Bratunac, from before the war, and Sinisa Glogovac, who has been interviewing prisoners at the white house, says, Oh, hey, here is a tip, since I know you're from Bratunac, the Muslims are heading off in that direction, towards Kladanj. That's the way it happened?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no, no. It's not the way you presented it. But, essentially, and you know this very well, I don't need to explain this to you so many times, Ljubisa Borovcanin and his units were resubordinated to the Drina Corps and all his official communication and all the information that he was supposed to receive was -- he was supposed to receive along that chain. His acquaintances with people from the state security who worked in that area enabled him to receive that information directly from them. According to their rules, they were not supposed to give him that information directly but through the system of reporting that was used to provide information to me, and others in the ministry. That's how they were supposed to work. Because these state security employees were not part of the police or the army staff and they were not sent there and they were not resubordinated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: While Mr. Nicholls is looking at his document, one legal question, Mr. Kovac. Take the example of Mr. Borovcanin. While he was resubordinated to the army, was he not still duty-bound to report to -- back to the MUP or police what he had been doing at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In keeping with the law, from the moment when he was resubordinated to the army, he would be exclusively under their competence and all his reports would go to the higher command of the Drina Corps, the commander of the Drina Corps. From the viewpoint of his activities at the moment when he's resubordinated. As soon as units are resubordinated, they become part of the army, and they execute solely the orders of the superior corps, or perhaps the brigade if they were resubordinated to the lower level, depending on the order given and the area to which they were assigned. Thereby, the state organ of the Drina Corps was the one who was supposed to give them orders.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Your answer could be either yes or no. So your answer is no. So he was not duty-bound to report what he had been doing to the police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He was not duty-bound to do that at the time when he was resubordinated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: P02987, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: From Ljubisa Borovcanin, 13 July 1995, when he's resubordinated, from the -- to MUP Special Police Brigade, it says on the top, to Pale police staff, Vogosca police staff, Special Police Brigade Janja. On 12 July 1995 in the course of the day, a MUP combat unit composed of the second Special Police detachment, a MUP company of the Zvornik PJP, and a mixed company of the Janja MUP was engaged in offensive combat operations from the direction of Zuti Most toward Potocari. And then it says about how at 5.30 they sealed off Zuti Most and then proceeded along the road towards Potocari which, if this helps you remember, is why I asked if you knew that they were amongst the first units in. In Potocari we sealed off the main UN base where a throng of between 25.000 and 30.000 civilians had gathered, approximately 5 per cent of whom were able bodied men. A part of the MUP forces was involved in the organisation of the evacuation of civilians from Srebrenica to Kladanj. As we had received information from state security that all able bodied Muslims from Srebrenica had set out on a break-through towards Konjevic Polje and further towards Tuzla, I urgently dispatched our forces with the support of hardware to seal off the Kravica-Konjevic Polje road where they spent the night. In the night between 12 and 13 July 1995, this armed Muslim group launched an attack on the direction of Konjevic Polje. In the combat that lasted several hours and which continued through the day, the enemy had more than 200 dead and we captured or had surrendered to us around 1500 Muslim soldiers. The number increases by the hour. According to all indications, the number of Muslim soldiers who did not manage to break through is on the rise -- who did not manage to break through, and is approximately between 5.000 and 6.000 which means that we have intense combat ahead of us. I hope that we will successfully carry out this task also, deputy commander, the Special Police Brigade, Ljubisa Borovcanin. Reporting his -- comprehensively reporting his military activities in the last two days while resubordinated; right?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he may report. It's up to him whether he will report or not. But he doesn't have the obligation to report. He's exclusively under the command of the army when he's carrying out these activities. And how he carried them out, you saw during the whole trial, you got all the explanations as to what he did and how he worked. The MUP got this for information and they sent these reports whenever they wanted, if they wanted. They didn't send these reports because it required any action from the MUP. He was not under the MUP command. He provided us with information. He gave us reports. But he was not under our command. He did not have the obligation to send this. He could have but he didn't have to.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You don't need to say in every question I ask you the MUP was not -- he was not under MUP command, okay?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it is necessary because you clearly want to involve MUP in a commanding role in these activities, which is completely untrue. We had different tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: As the deputy minister of the MUP and Borovcanin's superior at the time, I can see why you worry about that, but you don't need to answer every single question that Borovcanin wasn't under your command at the time. Are you seriously saying it's completely optional to report for the MUP, when they are resubordinated, Borovcanin can just decide whether or not the Ministry of the Interior should know that his MUP units have 1500 prisoners and are taking more by the hour?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Shall I hear your objection in the absence of the witness?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: I may say it in English if you want.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I think I'm not convinced that Mr. Kovac does not speak any English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before -- without going into detail, could you tell me just in a summary matter what it is about?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: It's pertaining the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You can speak in the B/C/S but just without telling the detail of your -- the merit, just tell us what it is about. So I will -- before we need to decide whether the witness is to be excused or not, tell me what it is about.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It has to do with the number and the nature of this report about the capturing of these 1500 men who captured them and whom they surrendered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. I think it can be raised -- discussed in your re-examination. Objection overruled. Please continue, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: So you can answer the question. It's completely optional when Mr. Borovcanin has captured or surrendered around 1500 Muslim soldiers and the number is increasing by the hour. It's completely optional whether he can -- should report that up the chain to the MUP?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let's not confuse the subject of reporting and his action. If it indeed happened that he took these people prisoner, which I doubt because this information was often inaccurate and it was written just like that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Kovac, I don't think that was part of the question. The question was whether it's optional on the part of Borovcanin to report or not.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was not optional to report. If he had any prisoners, he had to report his superior officer at the command of the Drina Corps. That's what he had to do. To report to the MUP in parallel was optional. He could have done that but not -- he didn't have to. It's one thing whether he had any prisoners or not and it's a completely different matter what was going on in a certain area. But you are linking decisions about how to treat particular prisoners and the subject of reporting. One thing is information as to what to do next. He had to get that from the Drina Corps. And the reporting --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'm stopping you now. I didn't ask you anything about treatment of these prisoners. I will but I didn't. Stop building into my questions questions I haven't asked you that you want to answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd request a break five minutes early, if it's not inconvenient, because I'm going to move on to something different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No difficulty with that. We will have a break for half an hour and resume at 5 to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's continue, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Could you please close your statement, not look at it for a moment. Thank you. 13 July 1995, in the afternoon, according to the president's appointment book which is P02242, I'm not going to bring that up, you meet with President Karadzic from 15.50 to 16.10, and you spend that time just discussing ammunition problems in Sarajevo; is that right?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That's it?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Nothing about Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. So this is the day that Borovcanin's reported that 1500 prisoners are being taken and the number is increasing. This is after you've sent the dog unit to Srebrenica. You remember that you sent the Doboj unit to Srebrenica on the 13th, you issued the order, Doboj PJP?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not correct. I sent the Doboj unit as assistants for protecting the town of Zvornik to the centre of the security services of Zvornik, not to the Srebrenica theatre of war. And they were 500 metres above the town of Zvornik because it was being threatened by the groups that were entering the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. You sent Doboj PJP to Zvornik, correct. That's P05146. Now, you've been informed about 1500 prisoners, Karadzic has been informed by the VRS about prisoners being taken, Vasic has reported to you about the situation, and you have no words whatsoever to say about what the MUP are doing in Srebrenica or what's happening in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, for two reasons: One is the law. They are resubordinated to the army, and any kind of reporting of mine would not have been correct or --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters did not understand the other word.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The second reason was that I opposed the engagement of units because of the real danger in Sarajevo, whereas the theatre of war, as such, was not a problem. However, a problem was made out of the way in which prisoners of war were treated. This was after the operation. This was 20 years later.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. P04942, please. This is from Vasic to the Ministry of the Interior on 13 July. I'm not going to go through it all. He's reporting: 1, we urgently need ten tonnes of petrol; 2, killing of about 8.000 Muslim soldiers who we blocked in the woods near Konjevic Polje. Fighting is going on. This job is being done solely by the MUP units. Send the Srbinje or Doboj special detachment to Konjevic Polje. You don't discuss Srebrenica because there were no problems in Srebrenica, only in Sarajevo; right?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I've already said what I had to say about these statements of yours and the terminology, liquidation, et cetera. This is not correct. This is panic stricken because he had quite a few Muslim soldiers who were on the move near Zvornik, Milici, and this is an arbitrary statement of his. Especially the term liquidation that he used. That is absolutely not doable. It was not carried out. And it is terminologically incorrect. And I have already said what I had to say about that, and he did not say what he had to say about that. I could not suggest to him how he should report. He reported the way he reported, and this is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. You just said "panic stricken." Panic stricken. The MUP is reporting to you that it is panic stricken. You're meeting with the Supreme Commander. That's not important enough to raise; right? Let me rephrase that. Let me make it clear. You meet --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection. Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The translation is the killing of 8.000 Muslims, whereas the liquidation of some group in military terminology is not killing. So this is the hundredth example of the translation is not good, the translation into the English language. The liquidation of a group in military terms does not mean killing and it was translated as killing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Let's go.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You meet with Karadzic on 13th, 14th and 15th of July; correct? It's in your statement; correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: On none of those days did you discuss Srebrenica; right?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't want that topic, and he didn't ask me, and I did not bring up the topic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Let me read you a portion of your testimony from the Jevic case. This is 65 ter 25516, English 24 to 25, B/C/S 25 to 26: Prosecutor -- well, he asks you, to make this shorter, about the dispatch you just talked about, regarding the 8.000 Muslims, however we want to qualify it, that Vasic -- that I just showed you. And he asks you: Did any of the dispatches give you grounds to go into the field and verify the situation? On the 13th, speaking of the 13th July. You: The main reason for my going in the end after they finished those operations was the direct order from the president of the republic, and it was my obligation as a policeman to visit the terrain, set up a police station in the generally chaotic situation to protect property, and introduce some police order after all the military activity. So I went into the field acting on orders of the president of the republic and with the intention of finding out about the situation in the town and the state of industrial facilities. We immediately set up a police station in order to establish order. This was my motive for going to that area. Do you stand by that sworn testimony?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: On the 13th of July, after meeting with Karadzic in the afternoon, later on that day you were in Vlasenica; correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went in the direction of Zvornik and Bijeljina and I passed through Vlasenica, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. You testified about it lots of times and in many statements. You met -- this is the short question: You met with General Mladic in Vlasenica on 13 July.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. His soldiers stopped me at the check-point in Vlasenica, and he asked to see him and I found him at the headquarters in Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Let me read to you some testimony from another of Mr. Karadzic's Defence witnesses in this case, Duga Puska, Zvonko Bajagic, 10 July.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: This is at T41161, Your Honours, 10 July 2013. I'll try to make it quick.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Mr. Bajagic is asked: General Mladic came to your house, didn't he, on 13 July? Yes, he did. Sat out on the terrace and had a beer; is that right? Yes. And then he discusses how the chief of the Vlasenica police comes by and said you were in Vlasenica, maybe at a hotel. And the witness says: Look, you refreshed my memory somewhat now. I'm rewinding this, trying to find some other details. I do remember the chief of police Milenko Masjorovic [phoen] told General Mladic when he got there that Tomo Kovac was in Vlasenica, either at the police station, the corps, or the hotel. He added the hotel. Okay. Thank you. So General Mladic asked you to go find Tomo Kovac, right, and check where he was? Yes. So you found him. You went and found Tomo Kovac? Yes. I'll skip ahead. After you found him General Mladic and Tomo Kovac had a meeting, didn't they? General Mladic sent me to find him and come to my house. The reason was that they should discuss something. Well -- question: Well, were you at this meeting weren't you, Mr. Bajagic? Well, in my mind, this wasn't a meeting. It was a short encounter. They discussed something. But out of courtesy, I didn't want to sit at the table with them. I assumed that as two commanders, commander of the Serbian army and the commander of the Serbian police, had something to talk about, so I went out while the two of them had a word. What they talked about, I don't know. And that's exactly what happened, isn't it, Mr. Kovac? That after leaving the office of the Supreme Commander, you, the commander of the police, went into the field as directed by Karadzic, you met with the commander of the army because you had something to discuss on 13 July, 1995; right?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is not right. You have several statements of mine. I did not meet with Mladic in Bajagic's house. At the check-point outside Srebrenica I was stopped, perhaps this Duga Puska Bajagic was with them, I cannot remember, and they stopped me then at the check-point and informed me that Mladic was looking for me and I did not stay at the hotel or the police station. So none of that is correct, none of that from that statement. It is correct that I was stopped and that I returned from that check-point and went to the command of the Drina Corps, and that is where I found Mladic. And I've stated that to you several times already, and I cannot go in this direction, Bajagic's statement. For me, he is an informal person, and I am not going to assess his statements and his memories, but this person never had an opportunity of seeing me and talking to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And while you're meeting with General Mladic that afternoon, having left the president's office after 4.00 p.m., that's while the Kravica warehouse executions are going on, isn't it? You know that.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, I did not know that and I could not have known that. This was not a meeting with Mladic. They stopped me and I went to this command and you have my statement as to how I found them at that command. If necessary, I can speak about that too now. I shall speak about it, if you ask me to do so. Do you want me to speak about that? How this evolved?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Let me summarise it quickly and see if -- you tell me if I get it right. Mladic saw you, he was drunk, he was bragging about taking Srebrenica, I think in your interview with me you said you stayed there and had a beer, and then you left.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I did not drink beer. They drank beer. Valjevsko Pivo, that was the beer that they were drinking, and they were rather drunk. This was bragging. And I left rather quickly because they were not really asking me for anything, because, I repeat, they stopped me at the check-point and this was characteristic of Mladic sometimes. This was not a friendly or a collegiate gesture. I visited with them briefly. I saw that they were drunk, they were bragging that they had taken Srebrenica, and that was it. They wanted me to congratulate them and that was the only conversation there. So there was no agreement reached. There was no discussion. It was impossible to discuss anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Right. It's impossible to discuss anything at the Drina Corps command with General Mladic. You -- he called you up there, then, for no reason; right? Nothing? Just to brag.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's right. That's the condition that they were in. There were several officers there. Krstic was there too. He was visibly in a good mood and drunk, and --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You answered the question. You said, well, that's right. That answered the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President, I don't think that's fair. If he wants to elaborate he should be allowed to.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, he -- he --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's go on. He answered the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could I have P05376, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Sir, this is an intercept from 19.45 on 13 July. It's somebody called X calling from General Krstic. I'm looking for Ljubisa who has gone Bratunac. Because I don't have much time I'm not going to go through it all. But X says, is that right? Y says, Yes. Those from Janja are here. X says, Okay. Y says, And the ones from Doboj, are they supposed to arrive? X says, Yes. Y, And, now, what shall I do with them? Well, you have to check about that with -- Y, because I've left it to -- in fact, to Ljubisa to plan it. And so whenever I need to I can send it off in that direction. Okay. That's it. Have Ljubisa call me at General Krstic's. Okay. You know where it is. I know. So doesn't that look to you like there is somebody at Krstic's working on the MUP coming from Doboj and Bijeljina, the Doboj units you ordered into the field? Was that -- was that you on this intercept saying have Ljubisa call me at Krstic's, since you were at Krstic's that day around that time?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, it wasn't me.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. And then, after you leave Vlasenica, you say in your statement that you went to Bijeljina, and I won't argue about that, but we agree you spent the night of the 13th at the Vidikovac hotel in Divic, in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And the Vidikovac wasn't just a hotel, the MUP used it as a check-point; right?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Not as a check-point. It was used for some other work that had to do with organisation of the procurement of ammunition, fuel, food and other supplies. It was impossible to use it as a check-point because it is separate. I was interested in those days for things that were needed for Sarajevo, and that's why I was there, that's why I spent the night there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is on the Drina, on the border, and --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: We all know where it is. The -- so the MUP for whatever purpose, and you've said this before, have offices there or have worked out of there, the Vidikovac?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were people there who worked in the department for material and technical resources. That's where they were staying. It was specifically these people who were there at that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, after this night, after you've been at Vlasenica with General Mladic, you know that there was a meeting, Vasic tells you about it later, a meeting between Vasic, Beara and Deronjic in Deronjic's office; right?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I did not see Vasic that night. I saw him only on the following day in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'm not asking you if you saw Vasic. Maybe it's a miscommunication. You know that late at night on the 13th of July, Vasic was in Deronjic's office with Beara and Deronjic at some point; right?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no. I was not informed about that, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. You're learning that from me today for the first time? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Don't -- don't -- let us not confuse things. One thing is what we all found out later, after what happened in Srebrenica, and it's a different thing what I knew between the 13th and the 14th. Between the 13th, 14th, I didn't know anything about that, and as for what we found out later on, both you and I can -- well, I mean I know over these 20 years I found out what happened, and --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Stop. You need to listen to my questions more carefully. I said -- well, let's see if we -- you know I meant now -- you know there was meeting, right, so we can stop this. We agree. You know now as you sit there today that Vasic, Deronjic, and Beara met in Deronjic's office on the night of the 13th; right? You know that now.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know now that you presented that to me precisely. At that time I was not interested in that activity and I didn't know about it. I mean, I -- no, I mean, what -- what is it that you want from this? That night I did not have any contact with Vasic, and I don't know what they agreed --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Deronjic is Karadzic's direct subordinate. Mladic is Beara's superior. Vasic is your subordinate. They all meet in Deronjic's SDS office that night, 13 July, to discuss what to do with all the prisoners in Bratunac. You're saying you didn't -- when did you find out about that meeting? First time.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I beg your pardon. Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Probably this -- could you put your question again?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Karadzic's newly appointed civilian commissioner for Srebrenica is meeting with Beara and meeting with Vasic in Deronjic's office. When did you find out about that meeting? You said you know about it now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You still have an objection?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This form of question, yes, but to imply that they met up to discuss the fate of the prisoners, that is unfair because we don't have any proof --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, no, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: There is clear evidence in the record about what happened at that meeting and that's our case.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: When did you find out about that meeting?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not informed about that meeting officially or unofficially, ever, from Vasic. So I was not informed about these meetings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, Mr. Kovac. It's very disappointing that you do not answer the question. The question was not whether you were informed at the time. When did you come to know that there was such a meeting, yesterday or ten years ago, two years ago? Or only now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At that time, I had not been informed about that meeting. I can be informed by reading documents as I prepare and say today and --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Stop. I'm sorry, stop. This is a very simple question. You're a lawyer. When did you first hear about this meeting?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until now -- well, I may have read about it in some documents but as for this meeting, especially not in this form that it was held -- I mean, I was not following meetings of Deronjic, Beara, Vasic. I did not receive this information. Let's be clear. I did not receive that information. In the form that you're putting the question, this is the first time I hear of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You have -- may I?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: No. Let me put it in this form. You've already told us you did hear about this meeting before today. This is very simple: When did you hear that Beara, Deronjic and Vasic met on the night of the 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say. I did not receive this information earlier on. I may have read it somewhere in the documents, but I cannot say. I didn't focus on that. I did not have information about that meeting, especially not in the form that you've been referring to it, as it had happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'm going to move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Let us move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, very briefly, I think this is easy. On the way to Zvornik, at Konjevic Polje, you saw Muslim prisoners on buses; correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And around 8.00 that night, 13 July, we are still on, is when the first prisoners go from Bratunac to Zvornik; right?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, according to this knowledge, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Right. So it's a pure coincidence that you go from the president's office to Mladic to Zvornik, and the prisoners go from Bratunac to Zvornik on the same night?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is no coincidence. This is the sequence of events as they evolved. Communication was normal for me on that route. The taking of prisoners in these operations and their transportation by buses to Zvornik, for me that was a legal situation, and that was not developing only at that moment. It was going on for a few days, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Right. So you knew -- so let's be clear. You knew that prisoners were being taken to Zvornik, not to Batkovic, to Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, yes, to Zvornik. It was a military barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Including the 1500 prisoners taken by the MUP that Borovcanin talked about that you knew about; right?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't go into the precise figures, how many the MUP had taken prisoners.
